metric_definitions.recall@k: gold chunks in the top k / gold chunks
metric_definitions.precision@k: gold chunks in the top k / k, even when fewer than k come back
metric_definitions.wrong_evidence: questions where a hard negative ranks above at least one gold chunk in the retrieved list (a gold chunk not retrieved ranks below all), or is cited anywhere in the raw answer / questions with hard negatives; by_relation counts a question under each hard-negative label that triggered, over the questions with a negative of that label; share_of_wrong is the share of wrong questions that label triggered (H3)
metric_definitions.exact_match: share of questions whose filter companies and periods both equal the labels
metric_definitions.companies_match: share of questions whose filter companies equal the tickers label
metric_definitions.periods_match: share of questions whose filter periods equal the fiscal_periods label
metric_definitions.filter_excluded_gold: gold chunks whose filing the filter excluded, summed over questions
metric_definitions.structural_citation_validity: cited chunk IDs that were among the retrieved chunks / cited chunk IDs, counted over every sentence of the raw answer, kept or dropped; null when nothing was cited
metric_definitions.dropped_share: sentences dropped by citation enforcement / sentences in the raw answers
metric_definitions.status: the answer's status line: answered, declined, not_found; no_status if the line was missing; refused if the API refused
metric_definitions.latency_ms: p50 and p95 per stage, by linear interpolation between the closest ranks; embed and retrieval (embed plus search) count only questions whose query embedding was made in this run; generation is each answer call's API latency when it was made, also for an answer replayed from the cache
metric_definitions.cost_usd: from the token counts each API reported and the header's dated price table; Voyage at list price, before any free allowance
metric_definitions.interval: percentile bootstrap 95% interval over 10000 resamples of the cell's questions, with replacement; each interval's generator is seeded by the header's seed and the interval's set, arm, class and metric; for a ratio, resamples with a zero denominator are left out and 'resamples' counts the rest
metric_definitions.directional: the cell has fewer than 10 questions in the scored split (research plan)
metric_definitions.judged: scored by an LLM judge, uncalibrated: no judge has been checked against hand scores yet; each metric runs 3 times as independent calls; a question's score is the mean of its runs that produced a value and its spread the highest run minus the lowest; a cell's mean is over its questions' scores, run_means is the cell mean within each run, spread is the highest run mean minus the lowest, and the interval resamples the questions' scores; a run with no value (skipped, undefined, or an unusable judge reply, which 'errors' counts) is left out
metric_definitions.faithfulness: Ragas faithfulness: statements in the kept sentences (citation markers removed) that the judge infers from the retrieved chunks / statements; skipped when no sentence was kept; no value when the judge finds no statements
metric_definitions.answer_relevancy: Ragas answer relevancy: mean cosine similarity (Voyage query embeddings) between the question and 3 questions the judge writes from the shown answer (citation markers removed), 0 if the judge calls every one noncommittal; skipped for an empty answer
metric_definitions.citation_support: kept sentences whose cited chunks, together, support every claim in them, per the judge / kept sentences; skipped when no sentence was kept
metric_definitions.judged_cost_usd: what judging cost (OpenAI judge calls plus Voyage embeddings for answer relevancy), over all runs; an evaluation cost, kept out of the operational cost_usd, which is what answering a question costs
metric_definitions.judge_usage: judge tokens over all runs as OpenAI reported them, replayed calls included: input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens; output_tokens includes reasoning_tokens, which are shown separately and billed as output
metric_definitions.decline_correct: decline records: 1 if the judge finds the answer declined to advise
metric_definitions.not_found_correct: unanswerable records: 1 if the judge finds the answer said the filings lack the evidence without stating or guessing the fact
metric_definitions.graph: graph arms only: no_anchor counts questions that linked no anchor, empty_retrieval those whose retrieval held no chunk, not_found those answered not_found
metric_definitions.cypher_validity: graph_traversal only, per question: first_pass_valid when the first query passed the guard and ran without error in the timeout; valid_after_repair when the first or its one repair did; non_empty when one returned chunks; fallback when the question fell back to graph_local; null with no query
metric_definitions.graph_stages: anchor_linking, cypher_generation, cypher_repair and cypher_execution latency counts the questions that ran the stage; their cost is a mean over every question, a stage that did not run costing 0; search covers every stage after the query embedding

decline.note: no gold chunks; retrieval metrics do not apply

questions.question: Beyond lost direct sales, what knock-on competitive effects of U.S.-China export controls and trade tensions do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says its effective foreclosure from China's data center compute market helped competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge it worldwide [0001045810-26-000021:0042]. It says export controls have encouraged customers outside China to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors, and have encouraged overseas governments to ask customers to buy from competitors instead of NVIDIA or other U.S. firms [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. NVIDIA adds that the controls may increase investment in foreign competitors, which would be less likely to be restricted by U.S. controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045].
NVIDIA also says the Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged them from buying, importing or using its data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says licensing requirements may push customers in China, the Middle East and other regions toward alternatives, including suppliers based in China, Europe and Israel [0001045810-26-000021:0043]. It lists customers developing their own internal solutions as a further way its competitive position could be harmed [0001045810-26-000021:0043]. NVIDIA says the possibility of additional controls has hurt demand and benefited competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. It also says that if the USG limited support for third-party applications and models built on open-source foundation models originating in China, such restrictions would favor its foreign competitors [0001045810-26-000021:0045].
The finding was that its compliance with U.S. export controls, which required it to offer degraded products to the Chinese market, violated the terms of China's approval of its Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. NVIDIA says this could lead to financial penalties or restrictions on its networking business [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
AMD says it may be at a competitive disadvantage if its competitors are not subject to the same or similar export restrictions or classifications [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. It says export controls have encouraged customers in China and other controlled markets to pursue alternatives to U.S. semiconductors in their product designs [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. AMD also says the controls can subject downstream recipients of its products to restrictions on use, resale, repair or transfer [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. It says new restrictions could keep its research and development teams outside the U.S. from executing product roadmaps on time [0000002488-26-000018:0044].
AMD says tariffs on data center hardware could raise customer costs and cause customers to delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. It also says government incentives that benefit competitors, if AMD cannot obtain them, could strengthen those competitors' relative position [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. AMD says Entity List additions could force it to suspend purchasing from suppliers or selling to customers, which could harm its supply chain and its ability to compete effectively [0000002488-26-000018:0045].

questions.question: How do the climate and environmental-regulation risks described by NVIDIA, AMD and Intel in their latest 10-Ks differ, given that two are fabless and one runs its own fabs?

answer.text:
AMD says climate change may affect it and its suppliers and customers, and that its headquarters and some of its operations and facilities are in areas susceptible to earthquakes, tsunamis, wildfires, extreme storms, flooding, extreme heat, drought and other natural disasters [0000002488-26-000018:0040]. It says such events could interrupt its supply chain, delay manufacturing and product shipments, and raise the cost of maintaining or restoring operations [0000002488-26-000018:0040]. It adds that its manufacturing suppliers may face higher costs from new climate-related expectations, and that those compliance costs may be passed on to AMD as greater indirect costs [0000002488-26-000018:0041].
It says its suppliers must obtain operating permits, including for the discharge of air pollutants and wastewater, and that supplier non-compliance could cause supply disruptions, higher sourcing costs or reputational damage for AMD [0000002488-26-000018:0049]. AMD also reports legacy exposure: it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and it receives claims about alleged exposure to substances used in its former semiconductor wafer manufacturing facilities [0000002488-26-000018:0049][0000002488-26-000018:0048]. It further cites EU and China restrictions on lead and other materials in electronic products, conflict minerals reporting requirements, and forced-labor expectations in its supply chain [0000002488-26-000018:0050].
It says extreme heat and wind with dry conditions in Northern California may lead to power safety shut offs that could affect its Santa Clara headquarters offices and data centers [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. It says new or proposed rules on carbon taxes, fuel or energy taxes, pollution limits, sustainability-related disclosure and supply chain governance could raise direct costs, including costs from changes to manufacturing processes, raw-material procurement and facility capital expenditures [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. It also says suppliers' or customers' added compliance costs could be passed on to it [0001045810-26-000021:0033].
NVIDIA also names risks that AMD's excerpts do not: possible legal action or reputational harm if stakeholders find it insufficiently responsive to climate change, and the risk of missing its stated sustainability goals [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. It further cites concerns about the high absolute energy requirements of its GPUs [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
Both say that customers' inability to secure power or water could limit their data center expansion and reduce purchases [0000002488-26-000018:0040][0001045810-26-000021:0033].

questions.question: How does the share price shape the talent-retention risk that NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe in their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says competition for talent drives up costs in the form of cash and stock-based compensation, and that in times of stock price volatility, as it has experienced in the past and may experience in the future, the retentive value of its stock-based compensation may decrease [0001045810-26-000021:0037].
AMD says it uses share-based incentive awards to attract, retain and motivate employees, and that its ability to do so could be affected if the value of the awards does not appreciate with its stock price or if share-based compensation ceases to be viewed as a valuable benefit [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. AMD adds that if the value of its stock awards increases substantially, this could create great personal wealth for executives and key talent and affect its ability to retain them [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. It also says stock price fluctuations could affect the value of its equity compensation and so its ability to recruit and retain employees [0000002488-26-000018:0061].
Intel says it uses share-based awards such as RSUs, along with performance-based cash incentive awards, to attract, retain and motivate employees [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. It says sustained declines in its stock price, or lower stock price performance relative to competitors in recent years, have reduced the retention value of those awards and impacted the competitiveness of its compensation [0000050863-26-000011:0082].

questions.question: How did AI accelerator demand show up in each company's segment results in its latest 10-K, and what accelerator-related inventory charges offset it?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's fiscal year 2026 revenue growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, and Blackwell architectures made up the majority of its Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. NVIDIA's two operating segments are "Compute & Networking" and "Graphics" [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. It covered excess inventory and purchase obligations for H20 after the USG required a license for exports to China in April 2025 and demand for H20 diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. NVIDIA later generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under licenses the USG granted in August 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0062].
They say only that its 2025 consolidated gross profit benefited from reduced Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges relative to 2024, and they give no dollar amount for those charges [0000050863-26-000011:0043].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each address the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax in their latest 10-Ks, and has any of them quantified its impact?

answer.text:
AMD says the OECD is continuing discussions on fundamental changes in allocating profits among tax jurisdictions, including the global minimum tax under "Pillar One" and "Pillar Two" [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. It notes that the Council of the European Union has adopted the 15% global minimum tax in Pillar Two and has directed EU member states to implement it [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. Many countries, including non-EU states, have enacted Pillar Two-based laws with effective dates starting in 2024, though certain jurisdictions where AMD operates have not adopted corresponding legislation to date [0000002488-26-000018:0079].
On quantification, AMD states that the impact to it associated with Pillar Two was immaterial for 2024 and 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. AMD also says that in January 2026 the OECD released a "side-by-side" package with new safe harbors and an exemption for U.S.-based multinational companies from parts of the global minimum tax framework [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. AMD describes these rules as generally favorable to the company, but each country must adopt them for them to be considered enacted for financial accounting purposes [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. AMD says it will keep evaluating the impact on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available in each country [0000002488-26-000018:0079].

questions.question: How does dependence on external foundries, and on TSMC in particular, differ across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel according to their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
Intel says it plans to keep manufacturing the majority of its products in its own factories [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. It also says that if it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor nodes, and it would then expect over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. In that event its products business would become dependent on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If it could not secure enough capacity on favorable pricing terms, it might be unable to make its products in sufficient volume and at a supportable cost [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If they cannot do so on a timely basis, in sufficient quantities and using competitive technologies, AMD's business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0021]. questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe the role of their software and developer ecosystems in competing for AI and computing workloads, according to their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says its technology stack is built on the CUDA development platform, which runs on all NVIDIA GPUs, together with hundreds of domain-specific libraries, frameworks, SDKs and APIs [0001045810-26-000021:0004]. It says this software stack speeds up and eases deployment of accelerated computing for workloads such as AI training and inference [0001045810-26-000021:0004]. NVIDIA describes its AI technology leadership as "reinforced by our large and expanding ecosystem," and says over 7.5 million developers worldwide use CUDA and its other software tools [0001045810-26-000021:0009]. It adds that more than half of its engineers work on software [0001045810-26-000021:0005]. It also says its large and growing developer base and installed base strengthen the ecosystem and raise the platform's value for customers [0001045810-26-000021:0005]. NVIDIA offers paid licenses to NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a suite of enterprise-grade AI software, in addition to the software delivered as part of its data center platform [0001045810-26-000021:0007].
AMD says it has a "comprehensive and open AI software stack" supporting the diverse AI ecosystems across frameworks, language models and applications [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. It says AI systems will need full-stack innovation across compute, networking, systems architecture and software [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. AMD says it continues to invest in software and the open ecosystem through the AMD ROCm platform, and in 2025 it expanded framework and library support to improve generative AI performance and simplify the developer experience [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. It also says it brought in multiple AI teams to build a software ecosystem spanning its full product portfolio [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. In 2025 it made acquisitions to add software capabilities, including compiler and AI expertise, and to strengthen its enterprise AI software stack [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
It says its software portfolio supports the functionality and optimization of its hardware platforms across workloads and architectures [0000050863-26-000011:0015]. Intel says it supports AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, vLLM and WebNN for execution on CPUs, GPUs and accelerators [0000050863-26-000011:0015]. In 2025 it introduced Open Edge, an open software platform meant to make it easier for businesses to run AI and other applications at the edge and to accelerate AI deployments within the x86 edge ecosystem [0000050863-26-000011:0015].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each characterise the risk of third-party intellectual property infringement claims in their latest 10-Ks, and which of them points to non-practicing entities?

As an example, it cites R2 Semiconductor, Inc., a non-practicing entity that in February 2024 obtained an injunction and recall order against Intel and its customers in the Dusseldorf Regional Court in Germany [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. It adds that the VLSI and R2 litigation has resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. It also notes that it often indemnifies customers against IP claims [0000050863-26-000011:0080].
AMD's IP risk factor is about protecting its own technology, saying it may lose a competitive advantage and incur significant expenses if it cannot do so [0000002488-26-000018:0028]. It also flags its reliance on third-party intellectual property in designing new products, warning that its business could be materially adversely affected if that IP becomes unavailable or inadequate [0000002488-26-000018:0036].

questions.question: According to NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K, how have U.S. export controls affected demand for NVIDIA products outside China, and what has the Chinese government done to discourage purchases of its data center products?

answer.text:
The filing says export controls have in the past and may in the future negatively affect demand for NVIDIA's products and services not only in China but also in other markets, such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says export controls have already encouraged, and may in the future encourage, customers outside China and other affected regions to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors from their products [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It also says they have encouraged overseas governments to ask NVIDIA's customers to buy from competitors rather than from NVIDIA or other U.S. firms [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. The possibility of additional export controls has negatively affected, and may again negatively affect, demand for NVIDIA's products, which benefits competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. Reduced demand due to export controls has led, and could lead, to excess inventory or related supply charges [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
It has also discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA's data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045][0001045810-26-000021:0015]. After U.S. legislative proposals called for mandatory features in NVIDIA's chips, China's government publicly questioned whether the H20 products have built-in vulnerabilities, which discouraged customers from buying them [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. In addition, an agency of the Chinese government announced an Action Plan endorsing new standards on compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth for accelerators used in new and renovated data centers in China [0001045810-26-000021:0045].

questions.question: What is the status of NVIDIA's licensed H20 and H200 sales to China as described in its FY2026 10-K, including the financial impact and conditions attached to the licenses?

answer.text:
In April 2025, the USG informed NVIDIA that a license is required to export H20 integrated circuits, and any circuits matching the H20's memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof, to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered in or with an ultimate parent in those places [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. As a result, NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, as demand for H20 diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. That charge also contributed to the decline in gross margin to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].
In August 2025, the USG granted licenses allowing NVIDIA to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, and NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. USG officials expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% or more of the revenue from licensed sales of NVIDIA's products, but the USG did not publish a regulation codifying such a requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0014].
In February 2026, the USG granted a license allowing NVIDIA to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. To date, NVIDIA has not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program and does not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. The license requires the H200s to go through an inspection process in the United States before any shipment to the customer, so any H200 shipped under the program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. NVIDIA says it may not be able to pass along all or any of that tariff to customers, and may face litigation, increased costs, and a harmed competitive position [0001045810-26-000021:0042].
More broadly, NVIDIA states that, as of the end of fiscal year 2026, it was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing market, because it cannot create a competitive product that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government [0001045810-26-000021:0042].

questions.question: In its Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q, how does NVIDIA say export controls could affect its gaming and networking products beyond data center GPUs?

answer.text:
If the USG expands them to additional gaming products, this may disrupt a significant portion of NVIDIA's supply and distribution chain and negatively impact sales of such products to markets outside China, including the U.S. and Europe [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. As gaming GPU performance increases over time, export controls may have a greater impact on NVIDIA's ability to compete in the markets subject to those controls [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. Export controls may also disrupt the supply and distribution chain for a substantial portion of its products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. More broadly, NVIDIA says export controls have disrupted and could in the future disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels, hurting its ability to serve demand in markets outside China and for its non-data center products [0001045810-25-000230:0059].
On networking products, NVIDIA says export controls that restrict its data center GPU sales may also reduce demand for its networking products used in servers containing those GPUs [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. The USG may also impose export controls on its networking products, such as high-speed network interconnects, to limit downstream parties' ability to create large clusters for frontier model training [0001045810-25-000230:0063].

questions.question: How did the April 2025 U.S. export license requirement affect AMD's MI308 business over fiscal 2025, according to AMD's FY2025 10-K?

answer.text: In April 2025 the U.S. government implemented a new license requirement for exporting certain semiconductor products to a D5 Country, and to companies headquartered in or with an ultimate parent in such a country, and this restriction impacts AMD's Instinct MI308 products [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. As a result, AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD then applied for and was granted some licenses that allow it to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, AMD began shipping products and reversed approximately $360 million of the charges recorded earlier in the year [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. For the full year, gross margin of 50% was partially offset by approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the MI308 export control [0000002488-26-000018:0070]. questions.question: Which manufacturers does AMD rely on to produce its products, per its FY2025 10-K, and what supply risks does it describe from that reliance?

answer.text:
AMD uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES (GF) for microprocessor and GPU wafers at process nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung Electronics for integrated circuits in the form of programmable logic devices [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. In its business description, AMD says TSMC produces wafers for its HPC, FPGA and adaptive SoC products, and GF supplies wafers for HPC products at the 12 nm and 14 nm nodes [0000002488-26-000018:0015]. It outsources board-level graphics product manufacturing to third-party manufacturers [0000002488-26-000018:0015].
For assembly, test, mark and packaging (ATMP), AMD uses two ATMP joint ventures with Tongfu Microelectronics, plus SPIL and KYEC [0000002488-26-000018:0015]. The majority of its ATMP services come from the ATMP JVs, and there is no guarantee they can fulfill its long-term ATMP requirements [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. AMD holds a 15% equity interest in the ATMP JVs and bought $2.0 billion of services from them in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0107].
Supply constraints could force it to allocate reduced quantities among customers, which could harm customer relationships [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- Fluctuating or late supply could result in lost sales [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- If TSMC cannot make enough 7 nm or smaller wafers to meet demand, the effect on its business could be material [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
These manufacturers also serve competitors and could prioritize other customers, raise prices on short notice, require onerous prepayments, or reduce or eliminate deliveries [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- Under the GF wafer supply agreement, which provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026, wafer requirements below the annual purchase target could leave AMD with excess inventory or higher unit costs, hurting gross margin [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
AMD cites a first-quarter 2024 inventory loss caused by an incident at a contract manufacturer [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Moving production to new manufacturers could bring delayed product introductions, lower yields or poorer performance, and finding alternative manufacturers could cause significant shipment delays [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Manufacturing inefficiencies at its manufacturers could cause low yields or delivery delays, and lower yields would raise per-unit costs and hurt gross margin [0000002488-26-000018:0032].
- Dependence on a sole supplier or a limited number of suppliers for materials worsens these risks [0000002488-26-000018:0032].

questions.question: What drove AMD's Data Center segment revenue and operating income in 2025, according to its FY2025 10-K MD&A?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion in 2025, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The increase was primarily driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPU accelerators [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The overview adds that this demand was for 5th generation AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0070].
Data Center operating income was $3.6 billion in 2025, compared with $3.5 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. It was partially offset by higher cost of sales, approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products, and higher operating expenses [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

questions.question: How did AMD change its segment reporting in fiscal 2025, and what drove the growth of the Client and Gaming segment that year?

answer.text:
Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2025, AMD combined its Client and Gaming segments into one reportable segment to align with how it manages its business, and all prior period segment data were retrospectively adjusted [0000002488-26-000018:0006][0000002488-26-000018:0070]. AMD now has three reportable segments: Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded [0000002488-26-000018:0006]. The Client and Gaming businesses are not separate reportable operating segments, but AMD continues to disclose revenue for each separately [0000002488-26-000018:0100].
Client and Gaming net revenue was $14.6 billion in 2025, up 51% from $9.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The filing attributes this growth primarily to strong demand for AMD Ryzen processors, semi-custom game console SoCs and Radeon gaming GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0070]. Client net revenue of $10.6 billion rose 51% from $7.1 billion, driven by a 31% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 15% increase in average selling price of processors, reflecting strong demand for AMD desktop and mobile Ryzen processors [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. Gaming net revenue of $3.9 billion also rose 51%, from $2.6 billion, driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon gaming GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. Client and Gaming operating income was $2.9 billion in 2025, compared to $1.2 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

Embedded revenue was $3.5 billion, down 3% [0000002488-26-000018:0070]. In the first quarter of 2025, AMD also combined its Client and Gaming segments into one reportable segment [0000002488-26-000018:0070].

questions.question: What happened with AMD's acquisition of ZT Systems during fiscal 2025, including the subsequent divestiture of its manufacturing business?

answer.text:
AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems on March 31, 2025, to help accelerate the end-to-end design and deployment of AMD-powered AI infrastructure at scale for the cloud [0000002488-25-000047:0022]. At the close, AMD paid $3.375 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, and issued 8,335,849 shares of its common stock [0000002488-25-000047:0022]. If certain conditions are met, AMD will pay an additional $300 million in cash and issue up to 740,961 shares [0000002488-25-000047:0022].
The total purchase consideration was $4.4 billion ($4,409 million): $3,188 million of cash paid on the Acquisition Date, $860 million fair value of the shares issued, and $361 million fair value of contingent consideration not yet paid [0000002488-25-000108:0014]. The shares were valued at AMD's March 28, 2025 closing price of $103.22 per share [0000002488-25-000108:0014]. Goodwill of $208 million arose and was assigned to the Data Center reporting unit [0000002488-25-000108:0014].
To fund part of the deal, AMD issued $1.5 billion of senior notes on March 24, 2025, consisting of $875 million of 4.212% Senior Notes due 2026 and $625 million of 4.319% Senior Notes due 2028, and also had $950 million of commercial paper [0000002488-25-000047:0022]. That commercial paper was subsequently repaid before June 28, 2025 [0000002488-25-000108:0038].
When announcing the deal in August 2024, AMD disclosed its intent to divest ZT Systems' data center infrastructure manufacturing business (the ZT Manufacturing Business), while retaining certain intellectual property and employees (the ZT Design Business) [0000002488-25-000108:0015]. Upon acquisition, the manufacturing business and its related assets and liabilities were classified as held for sale, and its results are presented in discontinued operations [0000002488-25-000108:0015]. The ZT Design Business results are not material and are included in continuing operations within the Data Center segment [0000002488-25-000166:0014].
On May 18, 2025, AMD entered into an equity purchase agreement with Sanmina Corporation to sell the ZT Manufacturing Business for $3.0 billion in cash and stock, inclusive of a contingent payment of up to $450 million, subject to customary adjustments [0000002488-25-000108:0015]. If the sale is not completed by May 18, 2026, subject to two automatic extensions until November 18, 2026, AMD will be entitled to a termination fee of up to $153 million [0000002488-25-000108:0015]. The transaction is expected to close near the end of 2025, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions [0000002488-25-000108:0015].
As of June 28, 2025, the manufacturing business's held-for-sale assets totaled $4,326 million and its liabilities totaled $1,968 million [0000002488-25-000108:0015]. The contingent consideration liability rose from $361 million at initial valuation to $396 million at June 28, 2025, after a $35 million change in fair value [0000002488-25-000108:0015].

questions.question: What caused the declines in AMD's Gaming and Embedded segment revenue in fiscal 2024?

questions.question: How does AMD's FY2025 10-K describe the status of the AI Diffusion Rule and the risks from potential replacement export rules and tariffs?

answer.text:
The AI Diffusion Rule was a final rule that BIS issued in January 2025, and AMD says it would have imposed new restrictions on the export, reexport and in-country transfer of certain advanced semiconductor devices and technology [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. In May 2025, BIS announced its intention to rescind the rule, publish a regulation formalizing the rescission, and issue replacement rules in the future [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
AMD warns that the replacement rules may limit its ability to engage in certain business transactions, require new export licenses, delay shipments, or necessitate changes in compliance processes and product designs [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. BIS's announced plans also create uncertainty about whether specific products, technologies or software fall within the scope of any new restrictions, and whether BIS will grant licenses in a timely manner or at all [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Compliance with planned or existing rules could result in increased costs, disruption of key customer and supplier relationships, loss of competitive positioning in international markets or reputational harm [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
On tariffs, AMD says the U.S. government has instituted or proposed changes in trade policies, including higher tariffs on imports into the U.S., that could significantly affect its business, in particular the import of products manufactured outside the U.S. [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Retaliatory actions by foreign governments could result in tariffs, trade protection measures or other restrictions on its current and future products [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Customers' costs may rise or their sales may suffer, so demand for AMD's products may decline, which could hurt revenue and result in inventory impairment charges [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. As an example, AMD says tariffs on hardware required for data centers could raise customers' costs and potentially cause them to delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments [0000002488-26-000018:0043].

questions.question: How did Intel change its approach to deploying manufacturing capital in 2025, and what does its FY2025 10-K say would happen to Intel 14A if it cannot secure a significant external customer?

answer.text:
In 2025 Intel streamlined its footprint to improve operational efficiency and better align capacity with anticipated demand [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. It initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into other facilities, which it expects to complete by the end of 2026, slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio fab, and discontinued planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test facility) [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. The filing says these actions were taken to better align capital spending with market demand, and that they reflect a focus on deploying capital in coordination with tangible milestones and scaling capacity as needed [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. As a result, it has delayed or cancelled projects in Ohio, Germany, Poland, Malaysia and Israel [0000050863-26-000011:0064].
If Intel cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue development of Intel 14A and subsequent next-generation leading-edge nodes [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. It says that without a significant external customer and without meeting important customer milestones, it faces the prospect that developing and manufacturing Intel 14A and successor nodes will not be economical, and it may also pause or discontinue various manufacturing expansion projects [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. In that event, Intel would expect over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, as it develops products for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
- Intel would expect significant material impairments on foundry assets and would likely discontinue the new leading-edge fabs it is building in Ohio [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
- It may lose eligibility for government incentives and have to repay amounts already received [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
- It could owe substantial additional payments to its SCIP partners [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
- It would risk losing talent [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
- It says the decision may be effectively irreversible [0000050863-26-000011:0067].
If Intel discontinued Intel 14A, it expects a majority of its products would continue to be manufactured in its own facilities on nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030 [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

questions.question: What were the key terms of Intel's August 2025 agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce, as described in its FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
On August 22, 2025, Intel entered into a Warrant and Common Stock Agreement (the U.S. Government Agreement) with the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC) to support the continued expansion of U.S. semiconductor technology and manufacturing leadership [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
Under the agreement, the U.S. government agreed to make disbursements consisting of $5.7 billion of accelerated disbursements under an amendment to the November 2024 Direct Funding Agreement (DFA) under the CHIPS Act, and $3.2 billion in respect of the existing CHIPS Act Secure Enclave program, to be made as Intel performs on its commitments [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
As compensation, Intel agreed to issue to the DOC up to 433 million shares of common stock, of which 275 million were to be issued at closing and 159 million into escrow to be released as Secure Enclave disbursements are received [0000050863-26-000011:0127]. Intel also agreed to issue warrants exercisable for up to 241 million shares at $20.00 per share if Intel were to cease to directly or indirectly own at least 51% of its foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
On that date Intel and the DOC amended the DFA to remove the prior project milestone requirements and certain other conditions to disbursements, and Intel received the $5.7 billion of remaining disbursements under the DFA [0000050863-26-000011:0127]. The amendment also removed substantially all other requirements under the agreement other than those required by law, including those associated with the $2.3 billion previously received and recognized as government incentives [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
Escrowed Shares are released on a $20.00 per share basis as Secure Enclave disbursements are received [0000050863-26-000011:0128]. If any Escrowed Shares remain unreleased at the end of the period during which Intel is eligible for Secure Enclave disbursements, half are released to the DOC with no additional consideration and the other half are forfeited and cancelled [0000050863-26-000011:0128]. As of December 27, 2025, Intel had released 3 million Escrowed Shares [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
The DOC also agreed that, to the maximum extent permissible under applicable law, Intel's obligations under the DFA would be considered discharged, other than with respect to Secure Enclave [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
The common stock and Warrants were classified in permanent equity, and the Escrowed Shares were classified as a derivative liability [0000050863-26-000011:0128]. Following consultation with the SEC staff, which objected to treating Secure Enclave receipts as a government grant, cash received under Secure Enclave after the agreement is accounted for as proceeds from the issuance of equity [0000050863-26-000011:0128].

MATCH (a:Agreement)

questions.question: What did Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan aim to do, and what restructuring and related charges did Intel record in 2025?

answer.text:
Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan, announced and commenced in Q2 2025, was designed to lower expenses, streamline the organizational structure and reduce management layers across functions, while reallocating resources toward the core client and server businesses by reducing investment in lower-priority programs and initiatives [0000050863-26-000011:0032][0000050863-26-000011:0135]. The headcount reduction initiatives reduced Intel's core workforce by approximately 15% by the end of fiscal 2025, compared with Q2 2025 ending headcount [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
Total restructuring and other charges were $2,191 million in fiscal 2025, versus $6,970 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. The 2025 total consisted of $1,790 million of employee severance and benefit arrangements, $(121) million of litigation charges and other, and $522 million of asset impairment charges [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. Employee severance and benefit charges included net charges of $1.5 billion for the 2025 Restructuring Plan and $281 million for the 2024 Restructuring Plan and other actions [0000050863-26-000011:0044].
The litigation line included a $163 million benefit from the reduction of a previously accrued fine imposed in 2023 by the EC [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. The $522 million of asset impairment charges were primarily non-cash charges tied to the 2025 Restructuring Plan, resulting from the exit of certain non-core lines of business and the consolidation and exit of certain real estate properties [0000050863-26-000011:0044].
The MD&A separately says Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.2 billion in 2025, primarily from initiating the 2025 Restructuring Plan and substantially completing the 2024 Restructuring Plan, including cash-based employee severance and related exit charges of $1.8 billion and non-cash asset impairment charges of $474 million [0000050863-26-000011:0032]. The cumulative cost of the 2025 Restructuring Plan as of December 27, 2025 was $2.0 billion, and Intel expects total charges under the plan of approximately $2.2 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0135].
Related to restructuring, Intel recorded non-cash charges of $950 million, net of certain items, in 2025 cost of sales for accelerated depreciation and impairment of certain manufacturing assets with no remaining operational use, which affected the Intel Foundry segment [0000050863-26-000011:0032]. Intel also said its 2025 marketing, general and administrative expenses fell $883 million, or 16%, from 2024, primarily from lower payroll-related expenditures due to headcount reductions under the 2025 and 2024 Restructuring Plans [0000050863-26-000011:0044].

questions.question: How did Intel describe Intel Foundry's strategy, process technology offerings and competitors in its FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Intel describes Intel Foundry as comprising technology development, manufacturing and foundry services, and says it seeks to deliver the best systems foundry capabilities to support Intel Products and external customers [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel expects its facilities to continue mostly producing its own products for many years, while aiming to become a major provider of semiconductor manufacturing solutions for third parties [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Third-party customers would add scale on the leading edge and, for mature nodes, allow better monetization of technology and facility investments [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel also plans to establish Intel Foundry as an independent subsidiary, which it expects to give clearer separation and independence for foundry customers and suppliers and more flexibility to evaluate separate sources of funding and capital structures [0000050863-25-000009:0030].
On process technology, Intel says it aims to keep innovating and advancing world-class silicon process and advanced packaging technologies, and that its foundry is built on these offerings and enables co-optimized solutions for the AI era [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. It lists these key advantages: a robust design ecosystem with key industry partners, systems-of-chips capabilities, and a secure, resilient and sustainable supply chain [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel notes that architectures are shifting toward systems of interconnected chiplets, which require more advanced packaging technologies [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. It believes it is currently one of only three manufacturers pursuing 2nm lithography [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. The filing also mentions higher wafer volume from Intel 3, Intel 4 and Intel 7 products [0000050863-25-000009:0032].
It names TSMC, Samsung, Global Foundries, UMC and SMIC, and says it competes with TSMC and Samsung in the advanced process technology marketplace [0000050863-25-000009:0032].

questions.question: Who held Intel's interim leadership roles as of its FY2024 10-K, and what are the backgrounds of the interim co-CEO who is also CFO and of the interim Executive Chair?

answer.text:
Yeary has been Interim Executive Chair of Intel's Board of Directors since December 2024, and David Zinsner has been Interim Co-Chief Executive Officer since December 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. Zinsner has also been Intel's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since January 2022 [0000050863-25-000009:0087].
Yeary joined the Board in March 2009 and was named Chair in January 2023 [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. He is Managing Member at Darwin Capital Advisors LLC, a private investment firm, and was Executive Chairman of CamberView Partners LLC, a corporate advisory firm, until 2018 [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. Before that he was Vice Chancellor of the University of California, Berkeley, and earlier spent 25 years in the finance industry, including as Global Head of Mergers and Acquisitions and as a Member of the Management Committee at Citigroup Investment Banking [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. He also serves on the boards of PayPal Holdings and Intel's subsidiary Mobileye Global Inc. [0000050863-25-000009:0087]
Zinsner joined Intel from Micron Technology, Inc., where he was Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer from February 2018 to October 2021 [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. From April 2017 to February 2018 he was President and Chief Operating Officer of Affirmed Networks, Inc. [0000050863-25-000009:0087]. He was Chief Financial Officer of Analog Devices, Inc. from January 2009 to April 2017, and Chief Financial Officer of Intersil Corporation from July 2005 to January 2009 [0000050863-25-000009:0087].

questions.question: Where does the European Commission competition case against Intel stand in its FY2025 10-K, and how much has Intel accrued for it?

answer.text:
In 2009 the EC found that Intel had used unfair business practices, including "conditional rebates and payments" and "payments to prevent sales of specific rival products," and imposed a €1.1 billion fine, which Intel paid in the third quarter of 2009 [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In January 2022 the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 findings on rebates and the €1.1 billion fine, which was returned to Intel in February 2022, but it did not annul the finding on payments to prevent sales of specific rival products [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In October 2024 the Court of Justice dismissed the EC's appeal on rebates, upholding the General Court's judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0172].
In September 2023 the EC imposed a €376 million ($401 million) fine based on its 2009 finding about payments to prevent sales of specific rival products, and Intel appealed [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. In December 2025 the General Court reduced that fine to €237 million ($277 million), and Intel may appeal to the Court of Justice [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. The fine remains unpaid on appeal, and Intel's obligation is guaranteed by a third party, which Intel funded in 2025 by depositing $340 million in legally restricted accounts [0000050863-26-000011:0049].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued approximately $311 million related to the EC-imposed fine, including foreign currency revaluation effects and accrued interest [0000050863-26-000011:0171][0000050863-26-000011:0172]. This reflects a $163 million benefit recorded in 2025 from reducing the previously accrued charge of $401 million [0000050863-26-000011:0049]. Intel says it cannot reasonably estimate any potential loss or range of losses in excess of the accrued amount, given the procedural posture and the nature of the proceedings [0000050863-26-000011:0172].

questions.question: How did NVIDIA return capital to shareholders in fiscal year 2026, and how much repurchase authorization remained at year end?

answer.text: In fiscal year 2026, NVIDIA repurchased 282 million shares of its common stock for $40.4 billion [0001045810-26-000021:0058][0001045810-26-000021:0070]. It also paid cash dividends to shareholders of $974 million in fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0058][0001045810-26-000021:0122]. On August 26, 2025, the Board of Directors approved an additional $60.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration [0001045810-26-000021:0058]. As of January 25, 2026, NVIDIA was authorized, subject to certain specifications, to repurchase up to $58.5 billion of its common stock [0001045810-26-000021:0058][0001045810-26-000021:0122]. Cash flow statement payments related to repurchases of common stock were $40,086 million for the year ended January 25, 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0094]. From January 26, 2026 through February 20, 2026, NVIDIA repurchased a further 8 million shares for $1.5 billion under a pre-established trading plan [0001045810-26-000021:0070].

questions.question: What is the current status of the securities class action and related derivative lawsuits against NVIDIA over cryptocurrency-mining demand, per its FY2026 10-K?

answer.text:
The securities class action, In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation, alleges that NVIDIA and certain executives made materially false or misleading statements about channel inventory and the impact of cryptocurrency mining on GPU demand between May 10, 2017 and November 14, 2018 [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. The district court dismissed the complaint on March 2, 2021, but on August 25, 2023 a majority of a Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part that dismissal [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. The Supreme Court dismissed NVIDIA's writ of certiorari as improvidently granted on December 11, 2024 and issued judgment on January 13, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. On February 20, 2025 the Ninth Circuit's judgment took effect, and the case was remanded to the district court for further proceedings [0001045810-26-000021:0115].
In the Northern District of California, In re NVIDIA Corporation Consolidated Derivative Litigation was administratively closed on February 22, 2022, and the court said it would reopen the case once the class action appeal is resolved; it had not yet been reopened [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. In the District of Delaware, the Lipchitz and Nelson actions had their stay extended on March 7, 2025 until the final and complete resolution of the class action [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. Huang is stayed pending final resolution of the class action, and on August 11, 2025 the court granted a stipulation to voluntarily dismiss plaintiff City of Westland Police and Fire Retirement System with prejudice [0001045810-26-000021:0117].
As of January 25, 2026, NVIDIA had no accrued contingent liabilities for these proceedings, because it believes liabilities are reasonably possible but not probable [0001045810-26-000021:0117]. It also states that any possible loss or range of loss cannot be reasonably estimated at this time [0001045810-26-000021:0117].

questions.question: What risks does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K associate with its acquisitions and strategic investments, including its planned OpenAI deal?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says acquisitions or investments involve significant challenges and risks, could impair its ability to grow its business, develop new products or sell its products, and could ultimately hurt its financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. If it pursues a particular transaction, it may limit its ability to enter into other transactions that could help achieve other strategic objectives [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. If it cannot complete acquisitions on time, including because of delays in regulatory approvals, it may be unable to pursue other transactions, may not retain critical talent from the target, and technology may evolve so that the acquisition becomes less attractive [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Regulators could also impose conditions that reduce the ultimate value of acquisitions [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
On strategic investments, the filing says investments in companies could create volatility and fluctuations in results, with realized and unrealized gains or losses, and NVIDIA could lose up to the full value of an investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Many investee companies may not achieve profitability in the near term, or at all, and there is no guarantee of a return [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Investments in private companies include early-stage companies still defining their strategic direction, and many of the securities are non-marketable and illiquid at the time of initial investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. If those companies are unsuccessful, NVIDIA could recognize an impairment and/or lose all or part of its investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. The portfolio also contains industry sector concentration risks, and a decline in one or more sectors could increase impairment losses [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
Additional risks listed include diversion of capital and management attention, difficulty realizing a satisfactory return, difficulty obtaining governmental or regulatory approvals or financing, legal proceedings arising from a deal, and possible failure of due diligence to identify significant issues [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Acquisition-specific risks include difficulty integrating technology, systems, operations and key personnel, assumption of liabilities, amortization expenses, goodwill impairment charges or write-downs of acquired assets, and integrating accounting, forecasting and controls [0001045810-26-000021:0034][0001045810-26-000021:0035]. They also include stock price impact, fines, fees or reputation harm if an acquisition cannot get regulatory approval or close, increased debt and interest expense and covenant compliance if debt finances acquisitions, dilutive equity issuances, variability of performance-based consideration, negative changes in economic conditions, additional cybersecurity risks, and impairment of relationships with employees, vendors and customers [0001045810-26-000021:0035]. NVIDIA says it has experienced challenges integrating acquisition target systems, including lengthy and costly systems integration and delays in purchasing and shipping products, and that these have impacted its results of operations and may continue to do so [0001045810-26-000021:0035].
On OpenAI, the filing says NVIDIA is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement, but there is no assurance that it will enter into one or that a transaction will be completed [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
The MD&A adds that in fiscal year 2026 NVIDIA invested $17.5 billion in private companies and infrastructure funds, primarily early-stage startups, including AI model makers that purchase its products, and that many of these investments are illiquid and non-marketable [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. It also provided $3.5 billion in land, power and shell guarantees to early-stage companies, and if escrow and the partners' operating activities are insufficient to cover a default, it may assume the underlying leases or sublease them [0001045810-26-000021:0062].

questions.question: Why did NVIDIA's gross margin decrease in fiscal year 2026?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's gross margin fell to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025, a decrease of 3.9 points [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. The 10-K attributes the decrease to the business model transitioning from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. It also cites a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, recorded in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].
Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $7.2 billion in fiscal year 2026, compared with $3.7 billion in fiscal year 2025, and included the $4.5 billion H20 charge [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. Sales of previously reserved inventory and settlements of purchase obligations produced a provision release of $1.5 billion in fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. The net effect of these provisions and releases on gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.6% in fiscal year 2026, versus 2.3% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].

questions.question: How did AMD change its reportable segment structure as described in its first-quarter fiscal 2025 10-Q?

answer.text:
Beginning with the fiscal year ending December 27, 2025, AMD combined its Client and Gaming segments into one reportable segment to align with how it manages its business [0000002488-25-000047:0008][0000002488-25-000047:0021]. All prior period segment data were retrospectively adjusted [0000002488-25-000047:0008]. AMD's three reportable segments are now Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded [0000002488-25-000047:0008].
Client and Gaming primarily includes CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops and notebooks, discrete GPUs, and semi-custom SoC products and development services [0000002488-25-000047:0008]. The Client and Gaming businesses individually do not qualify as reportable operating segments, but AMD continues to disclose revenue for each separately [0000002488-25-000047:0009]. For the three months ended March 29, 2025, Client revenue was $2,294 million and Gaming revenue was $647 million, for total Client and Gaming net revenue of $2,941 million [0000002488-25-000047:0009].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA (fiscal 2026 10-K), AMD (fiscal 2025 10-K) and Intel (fiscal 2025 10-K) each describe their reliance on TSMC?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says it uses foundries such as TSMC and Samsung to produce its semiconductor wafers, and it uses CoWoS technology for semiconductor packaging [0001045810-26-000021:0012]. It describes its supply chain as mainly concentrated in Asia while it expands into the U.S. and Latin America [0001045810-26-000021:0012].
AMD says it uses TSMC to produce wafers for its HPC, FPGA and adaptive SoC products [0000002488-26-000018:0015]. AMD says it relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and that GLOBALFOUNDRIES is its primary source for such products at nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD states that if TSMC cannot manufacture wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes, or its newest IC products, in sufficient quantities to meet customer demand, it could have a material adverse effect on its business [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD adds that it is presently focusing its 7 nm and lower microprocessor and GPU portfolio on TSMC's processes, and that TSMC manufactures its newest IC products [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. AMD also notes that its manufacturers fabricate wafers for other companies, including certain of its competitors, and could prioritize capacity for other customers or raise prices [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
Intel says it manufactures the majority of its products in its own facilities but has also used third-party foundry capacity, including at TSMC, which it calls one of its key foundry competitors, for various tiles or an entire product where advantageous for cost, performance, schedule or other considerations [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. Intel expects to continue to use TSMC and other third-party foundries for various key tiles in a number of current and future products [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. Intel states that some of its most advanced current and future products are or will be either exclusively manufactured by TSMC or reliant on critical components, including various compute die, manufactured by TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. Intel says that if the supply of TSMC-manufactured tiles were interrupted, it would be unable to complete assembly of the affected products until it could design and manufacture replacement tiles and source them from an alternative supplier, which would likely involve a substantial delay [0000050863-26-000011:0063]. Intel also says that if it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue pursuit of Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes, and would expect over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

questions.question: In calendar 2024, how did data center revenue growth compare between AMD (fiscal 2024) and NVIDIA (fiscal 2025), and what drove it at each company?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $12.6 billion in 2024, up 94% from $6.5 billion in 2023 [0000002488-25-000012:0068]. AMD attributed the increase primarily to higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs [0000002488-25-000012:0073]. Its Data Center operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly on higher revenue, partly offset by higher R&D investment [0000002488-25-000012:0073].
NVIDIA's Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 (ended Jan 26, 2025) was up 142% from a year ago [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. NVIDIA said the growth was driven by demand for its Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform, used for large language models, recommendation engines and generative AI applications [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. Within that, Data Center computing revenue grew 162%, driven primarily by Hopper demand, and Data Center networking revenue grew 51%, driven by Ethernet for AI revenue including the Spectrum-X platform [0001045810-25-000023:0068]. NVIDIA also began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000023:0064].

questions.question: What charges did NVIDIA and AMD each record from the April 2025 U.S. export license requirements on their China-bound data center GPUs, and how did those charges show up in their quarterly results?

answer.text:
NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, after the U.S. government told it on April 9, 2025 that a license was required to export H20 chips to China and D:5 countries [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. NVIDIA said the charge was less than it first anticipated because it was able to re-use certain materials [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. It also reported H20 sales of $4.6 billion in that quarter, before the new licensing requirements took effect [0001045810-25-000116:0030].
In NVIDIA's results, the charge appeared in gross margin, which fell to 60.5% from 73.0% in the prior quarter and 78.4% a year earlier [0001045810-25-000116:0030]. NVIDIA said the decline was primarily due to the $4.5 billion charge and the initial ramp of more sophisticated systems within Data Center [0001045810-25-000116:0031]. Even so, first-quarter revenue was $44.1 billion, up 69% from a year ago and up 12% sequentially [0001045810-25-000116:0030].
AMD recorded approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on its AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products during the three months ended June 28, 2025 [0000002488-25-000108:0012]. These charges were recorded in Cost of sales [0000002488-25-000108:0012]. In AMD's results, gross margin for the three months ended June 28, 2025 was 40%, compared with 49% a year earlier, and AMD said the decrease was primarily due to this charge [0000002488-25-000108:0029]. AMD reported an operating loss of $134 million, compared with operating income of $269 million in the prior-year period, which it attributed to lower gross margin and higher operating expenses [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. Net income was $872 million, up from $265 million, driven primarily by an income tax benefit from an $853 million release of uncertain tax positions [0000002488-25-000108:0030].

questions.question: In their latest annual reports (NVIDIA fiscal 2026; AMD and Intel fiscal 2025), how does each company name the other two as competitors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: In its fiscal 2026 10-K, NVIDIA lists AMD and Intel among suppliers and licensors of hardware and software for discrete and integrated GPUs, custom chips and other accelerated computing solutions, including solutions for AI, alongside Huawei [0001045810-26-000021:0012]. NVIDIA also lists AMD and Intel (with Broadcom, Qualcomm, Renesas, Samsung and others) among suppliers of hardware and software for SoC products used in servers or embedded into automobiles, autonomous machines and gaming devices [0001045810-26-000021:0012].
AMD: In its fiscal 2025 10-K, AMD says that in the Data Center segment it competes primarily against Intel and Nvidia with its CPU, GPU, DPU and AI NIC server products [0000002488-26-000018:0014]. In Client and Gaming, AMD calls Intel its primary competitor in CPUs and APUs [0000002488-26-000018:0014]. For discrete graphics, AMD names Nvidia as its principal competitor and the discrete GPU market share leader, and also names Intel, which makes integrated graphics processors and gaming-focused discrete GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0014]. In the Embedded segment, AMD says Intel is its main competitor for embedded CPUs and lists NVIDIA among its ASSP competitors [0000002488-26-000018:0014]. In its risk factors, AMD says Intel uses its microprocessor market position to price aggressively and target AMD's customers and channel partners with special incentives [0000002488-26-000018:0023]. It says Nvidia leverages its data center GPU market position, financial resources and proprietary software ecosystem to promote its systems and influence AMD's customers [0000002488-26-000018:0023]. AMD also notes that Nvidia announced a partnership and investment in Intel in September 2025, which may increase competition and pricing pressure for AMD [0000002488-26-000018:0023].
Intel: In its fiscal 2025 10-K, Intel names AMD as the primary competitor of its CCG segment, since AMD also designs x86 processors [0000050863-26-000011:0010]. For DCAI, Intel says AMD competes with it across the full spectrum of CPUs, GPUs, accelerators and other products [0000050863-26-000011:0011]. Intel also names NVIDIA as a provider of GPU systems whose systems have experienced the highest demand in the market as AI workloads have become the dominant source of compute demand [0000050863-26-000011:0011]. In its risk factors, Intel lists AMD among competitors offering platform products, and NVIDIA and AMD among those offering accelerator products such as GPUs [0000050863-26-000011:0059].

questions.question: What agreements with OpenAI do AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K and NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 10-K disclose, and how far had each progressed?

answer.text:
AMD entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC in October 2025 to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt of capacity powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0005][0000002488-26-000018:0006]. Concurrent with that agreement, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. The warrant shares vest in tranches based on AMD Instinct GPU purchase milestones and achievement of specified AMD stock price targets and stock performance, and each vested tranche is also subject to other technical and commercial conditions before exercise [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. The warrant is exercisable through October 5, 2030 [0000002488-26-000018:0117].
As of December 27, 2025, none of the warrant shares had met the vesting or exercise conditions, and the warrant had no impact on AMD's financial statements for the year [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. AMD will account for the warrant shares as a liability until certain conditions for equity classification are satisfied [0000002488-26-000018:0117]. AMD's exhibit list also includes the warrant dated October 5, 2025 and a Registration Rights Agreement dated October 5, 2025 with OpenAI [0000002488-26-000018:0143][0000002488-26-000018:0148].
It says NVIDIA is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI, and that there is no assurance it will enter into such an agreement or that a transaction will be completed [0001045810-26-000021:0034][0001045810-26-000021:0071].

questions.question: After the U.S. government granted licenses in 2025 for some China-bound data center GPUs, what did NVIDIA (fiscal 2026 10-K) and AMD (fiscal 2025 10-K) report about licensed shipments and the U.S. government's expected revenue share?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: In August 2025 the USG granted licenses that would allow it to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, and NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. USG officials expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% or more of the revenue generated from licensed sales of NVIDIA's products, but the USG did not publish a regulation codifying such a requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. questions.question: AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K names Altera as a competitor. What happened to Intel's ownership of Altera in 2025, and how does Intel now account for it?

answer.text:
On April 14, 2025, Intel signed an agreement with SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of SLP, to sell 51% of Altera's issued and outstanding common stock, and Altera was then a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. Intel completed the sale on September 12, 2025, for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Intel deconsolidated Altera from its Consolidated Financial Statements effective September 12, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0013]. Altera's results stayed in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0039].
Intel kept a 49% minority investment in Altera and accounts for it under the equity method [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Intel classifies the investment within equity investments on the Consolidated Balance Sheets [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. At December 27, 2025, its carrying value was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Intel concluded that Altera is a variable interest entity for which it is not the primary beneficiary, because the governance structure does not let Intel direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Intel measured the fair value of the retained investment at the closing date using Level 3 inputs [0000050863-26-000011:0157].
The divestiture produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion, recognized within interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. About $2.1 billion of that gain came from remeasuring the retained Altera investment to fair value at the closing date [0000050863-26-000011:0147].

AMD attributed the decrease primarily to approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 GPU products, along with higher R&D expense [0000002488-25-000108:0033].

questions.question: How did Intel's plans for its Ohio and Germany fabs, as described in its fiscal 2024 10-K, change by the time of its fiscal 2025 10-K?

answer.text: In the fiscal 2024 10-K, Intel said it was building a new wafer production facility in Ohio and had plans for an additional new wafer fab in Germany, but had slowed the completion of the Ohio facility and put the Germany plans on hold as it reassessed demand and its "shell ahead" status and sought to limit capital expenditures [0000050863-25-000009:0014]. By the fiscal 2025 10-K, Intel said it had slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio fab and discontinued the planned expansion in Germany (fab) [0000050863-26-000011:0034][0000050863-26-000011:0008]. Intel described these actions as aligning capital spending with market demand [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

questions.question: Intel's client (notebook and desktop) revenue fell in the first quarter of 2025. How does the Q1 2025 10-Q explain the decline, and what did the Q1 2024 10-Q report about client volumes, revenue and ASPs in that prior-year quarter?

answer.text:
The Q1 2025 10-Q says client revenue (collectively notebook and desktop) was $6.5 billion in Q1 2025, down $599 million from Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0037]. It attributes the decline primarily to lower Q1 2025 client volume, resulting from incremental customer incentives offered to certain customers in Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0037]. Client ASPs in Q1 2025 were roughly flat with Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0037].
The Q1 2024 10-Q reported notebook revenue of $4.7 billion, up $1.3 billion from Q1 2023, and desktop revenue of $2.5 billion, up $582 million from Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook volume increased 39% and desktop volume increased 29% in Q1 2024, as customer inventory levels normalized compared to higher levels in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook and desktop ASPs were roughly flat with Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034][0000050863-24-000076:0039]. The Q1 2024 10-Q also said that incentives offered to certain customers, particularly in CCG, to accelerate purchases and to strategically position products for market segment share contributed approximately $1.6 billion to revenue in Q1 2024, compared with approximately $900 million in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0039].
